latin: Non inebriabitur per aliquem Bacchum, qui suae musae prius copulatus non fuerit.
translation: No one will be made drunk by any Bacchus who has not first been joined to his own Muse.
translation_note: 'copulatus' is rendered 'joined', keeping the verb's ordinary sense of union rather than a specifically marital one (farmer1998:26018).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch18, from Latin at farmer1998:26018
doctrine: The thesis holds that mystic intoxication by a given 'Bacchus' requires prior union with one's own Muse (farmer1998:26018). Farmer's note states that this thesis opens a series (starting at thesis 2.12) in which the several 'Bacchae' stand for different modes of will (farmer1998:26098).
context: The thesis belongs to the Orphic Hymns own-opinion series (farmer1998:25560). Farmer cross-references thesis 8>6, among the Zoroaster and Chaldean conclusions, which states that the Chaldean interpreters' sayings on the double intoxication of Bacchus and Silenus are perfectly understood through the Kabbalists' teaching on two wines (farmer1998:24842).
reception: Busi and Ebgi print the thesis's Latin text verbatim and cross-reference it, in their commentary apparatus, to their entry on the Muses (busi2014:24644; busi2014:17253).
historiography: Busi and Ebgi are the only source discussing this thesis in the material consulted; no scholarly dispute over its interpretation is recorded there (busi2014:24644).

quotations.text: Non inebriabitur per aliquem Bacchum, qui suae Musae prius copulatus non fuerit.

not_established: The content of Busi and Ebgi's entry on the Muses, to which they cross-reference this thesis: not established beyond the cross-reference itself (busi2014:17253).
